thread:
morgan: convene quick design on continuation/resume surface across py/ts/go 
priya: high level: avoid leaking runtime internals, keep ergonomics idiomatic per lang, and make retries explicit
jonas: concrete pain: paged unary endpoints want small stable tokens; streaming wants more live-state resume without forcing apps to store big blobs
liam: option 1: minimal token (opaque string). pros: easiest. cons: no partial resume, debugging is annoying, and we end up morphing token format often
priya: option 2: semi-structured token (versioned base64 JSON with {v, cursor, seq, meta}). SDKs expose helpers to parse if needed. pros: debuggable + server can evolve. cons: surface complexity + potential PII risk if we put too much meta
morgan: option 3: split surface: server returns a short-ttl ResumeHandle (opaque) plus optional Diagnostics object available via SDK fetchDiagnose(handle). SDKs can attach transient local state for streaming-only resumes
jonas: transport mapping:
- streaming (grpc/ws): keep lightweight in-SDK state and server-side KV; ResumeHandle just points to server slot
- unary/paged: include ResumeHandle in next page request body
liam: language ergonomics proposals:
- python: iterator abstraction that by default auto-resumes on transient errors. opt-in flags: resume_token=True to return token with each item, auto_resume=False to disable automatic retry
- typescript: async iterable + explicit resume token APIs (getResumeToken(), resumeFrom(token)). default is explicit (no magic auto-retry) to fit web patterns
- go: return small ResumeToken struct (fixed fields, no allocations) and ResumeFrom(token) functions. explicit is preferred in Go land
priya: retries semantics:
- streaming: SDK does best-effort transparent reconnect+resume for transient transport hickups (exponential backoff). expose callbacks so apps can detect resumptions
- paged/unary: do not auto-retry resumes across multiple pages unless user requests it (risk of duplicating side effects)
morgan: token format: must include a short "ver" field. server should support multiple versions and emit Deprecation headers when older tokens are used
jonas: privacy: tokens must never contain raw customer text. any metadata must be hashed/salted. telemetry mapping to trace ids ok, but only by reference (no PII)
liam: storage lifetime: default ttl 4 hours. enterprise may request longer via header/flag and audit control. document retention in SDK docs
priya: debug ergonomics: SDK dev mode can return a decoded view of the token for local debugging (only in dev mode)
ada-bot: (automated) reminder: change touches runtime handshake. coordinate with eng-runtime and update integration-tests and compatibility matrix
morgan: open questions:
- should we unify resume token API surface under a single module (e.g., client.resume)? or scatter per method?
- do we allow server-initiated invalidation events to be streamed to SDKs? (eg. server says handle expired)
jonas: my take: single well-documented Resume API on the client object is nicer for discoverability. server invalidations should surface via errors+well-typed enums
liam: implementation plan:
1) spec token v1 (base64+versioned json) + server acceptance layer
2) SDK stubs for py/ts/go with feature flags behind preview opt-in
3) runtime handshake changes and e2e tests
4) opt-in dev-mode debug decode
priya: i'll draft python+ts API stubs and a short compatibility note. liam can prototype go struct and perf check
morgan: ship timeline suggestion: API draft this week, runtime changes next week, SDK previews in two sprints. owners: priya (py/ts), liam (go), jonas (runtime coord)
ada-bot: (automated) please add a migration checklist issue and tag eng-runtime, security for token-format review
priya: noted. will create issues and assign. thanks all :thumbsup:
